semantic_votes.rationale: The sole-authority statement is explicitly limited to Analyzed Work and the implementation-preparation mode contract, preventing derived artifacts from competing with the accepted Brief.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies only while engineering-change-analysis produces or updates the current Engineering Brief for Analyzed Work.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain the Analyzed Work and mode-contract bounds and route protected-decision changes back through Brief revision.

semantic_votes.rationale: The template correctly classifies requests, source, tests, external evidence, and Specialist results as inputs rather than parallel operational analysis authorities.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies within the Engineering Brief template after source and Specialist evidence are incorporated into the current Brief.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep the input-versus-authority distinction adjacent to the incorporation rule and Brief update path.

semantic_votes.rationale: The statement is bounded by Analyzed Work and establishes one operational Brief authority, avoiding contradictory downstream acceptance, ownership, and placement decisions.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies to the current Engineering Brief produced for the active Analyzed Work lineage.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Preserve the Analyzed Work qualifier and require Brief regeneration when protected decisions legitimately change.

semantic_votes.rationale: Verbatim dispatch and prohibition on reselection preserve the analysis-owned First Executable Slice across Main and DAG projection boundaries.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies after the Engineering Brief has selected a complete and safe First Executable Slice.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep conflicts on slice content routed to an updated Brief and redispatch rather than downstream reinterpretation.

semantic_votes.rationale: The protected-field list correctly constrains derived artifacts from silently becoming competing authorities for accepted analysis decisions.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies to Task DAGs, Task Contracts, Implementation Handoffs, and Review Handoffs derived from a current Brief.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain the explicit protected fields and return any required decision change through analysis for Brief revision.

semantic_votes.rationale: Main's prohibition on regeneration or reinterpretation preserves the exact analysis-selected slice and prevents dispatch-layer semantic drift.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when Main dispatches the First Executable Slice selected in the current Engineering Brief.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Maintain verbatim dispatch and use the defined blocked-to-analysis path when the slice cannot be executed safely.

semantic_votes.rationale: The Task DAG is a projection surface, so forbidding slice reselection and protected-decision modification preserves correct analysis ownership.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies only to a Task DAG derived from an accepted current Engineering Brief for Analyzed Work.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep DAG authority limited to task decomposition, dependencies, scheduling, and integration ownership.

semantic_votes.rationale: Specialist evidence may inform placement or risk decisions, but the Brief must incorporate it before it gains operational effect.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies to Specialists invoked for unresolved structural choices during Engineering Brief preparation.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain explicit incorporation into the current Brief before Specialist conclusions affect implementation.

semantic_votes.rationale: The word only limits the section to material impact categories while still requiring direct and transitive consumer coverage.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when populating Contract, Data, and Failure Impact in an implementation-preparation Engineering Brief.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Preserve materiality as the inclusion boundary without omitting direct or transitive consumers.

semantic_votes.rationale: Prohibiting a parallel analysis authority prevents Specialists and derived artifacts from producing incompatible implementation decisions outside the current Brief.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies during implementation-preparation after source evidence and any Specialist result are reconciled into the Brief.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep one Brief authority and route legitimate decision changes through explicit Brief update and redispatch.

semantic_votes.rationale: An Implementation Handoff records execution evidence and must not overwrite the accepted decisions that authorized the implementation.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies to Implementation Handoffs for work dispatched from a current Engineering Brief First Executable Slice.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep the handoff evidence-only and return protected-decision conflicts to analysis before further execution.

semantic_votes.rationale: The rule correctly protects Brief-owned acceptance, ownership, placement, contract, rollback, and slice decisions from downstream derived artifacts.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies to all Task DAGs, Task Contracts, Implementation Handoffs, and Review Handoffs derived from the current Brief.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Maintain the enumerated protected boundaries and use Brief revision for any authorized change.

semantic_votes.rationale: A review agent cannot change its own assigned Effective Level because that would bypass the analysis and dispatch authority boundary.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies during implementation review when new risk evidence may invalidate the assigned Effective Level.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep self-upgrade forbidden and return newly discovered L4 or L5 risk through Main for recomputation.

semantic_votes.rationale: L4 retains one independent final implementation review while adding only risk-triggered gates, Specialists, or design-carried pre-review evidence.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when the authoritative execution-level contract sets Effective Level L4 for the implementation review.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain the base review and require every triggered specialist dimension without treating L4 as an automatic reviewer count.

semantic_votes.rationale: L3 preserves the full independent base review and adds JIT lenses only when concrete risk triggers make them relevant.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when the authoritative execution-level contract sets Effective Level L3 for the current implementation review.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep all base review dimensions mandatory and add rather than substitute any risk-triggered JIT lens.

semantic_votes.rationale: Resolving the task boundary, latest diff, every changed file, and reachable impact is the necessary first action for any bounded code review.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies whenever the code-review capability is selected for a task-local implementation or repair review.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep this front-loaded root rule and stop approval when any part of the review surface remains unresolved.

semantic_votes.rationale: The control plane must not assume unavailable host capabilities because unsupported diff or validation modes require fail-closed routing.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when host diff, validation, or utility no-edit capability is absent or unrecognized during Direct Task routing.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep capability inference prohibited and use the named utility no-edit capsule or unsupported-mode blocker.

semantic_votes.rationale: The flagged span is compact control-plane policy for authority, scheduling, review evidence, and closure states, not tutorial or explanatory teaching content.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: The detector applies only when root text teaches through examples or extended explanation rather than defining executable control contracts.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain the operational clauses and treat syntax markers, state values, and routing arrows as contract notation rather than tutorial signals.

semantic_votes.rationale: Focused proof must exercise the changed failure mechanism and consequential negative outcomes; broad green status cannot close an untested risk.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when code-review evaluates validation evidence for changed behavior and reachable failure outcomes.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep the rule in the root review sequence and state proof limits whenever focused mechanism evidence is unavailable.

semantic_votes.rationale: L1 and L2 still receive one independent final review covering the complete base matrix, so lower level does not remove Core dimensions.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when the authoritative execution-level contract sets Effective Level L1 or L2 for implementation review.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Retain the complete base matrix and do not treat the level as permission to omit any Core review dimension.

semantic_votes.rationale: A regression guard proves recurrence prevention only when it reproduces the causal trigger instead of merely testing adjacent correct behavior.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies only after an accepted defect, incident, review finding, or equivalent recurrence mechanism is known.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep the causal-trigger rule front-loaded and require explicit proof limits when safe reproduction is infeasible.

semantic_votes.rationale: The two-task threshold avoids ceremonial DAGs, while requiring every actual edge to represent a blocking fact preserves graph semantics.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when an accepted Brief contains at least two real tasks with evidenced dependency, parallel, integration, or release-order value.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep zero-edge parallel DAGs permissible and reject invented nodes, edges, cycles, or placeholder work.

semantic_votes.rationale: A risk-specific Specialist covers only its named lens, so it cannot substitute for the independent final review of the whole changed scope.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies whenever implementation review delegates a concrete risk dimension to a Specialist Skill.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep the review owner responsible for merging Specialist findings into the complete final implementation review.

limitations: This ballot reviews only the 23 packet-bound semantic candidates and their current source context; it does not replace readability, professional-completeness, release, real-host, or production evidence.
